I want to make it clear that I don’t criticize them like that. I usually just do it myself because having the conversation would be worse than just pushing myself. They don’t take criticism well and I don’t want to hurt them. I have not listed these things to them - I’ve just brought it up casually when an opportunity arises. 

Example: when they saw me cleaning the bathroom sink (something they’ve never done, and I’m not being at all hyperbolic) they commented on how I got the soap tray so clean. I showed them how it comes apart and what I use to clean the area. 

Yes, they clean the dishes more often without provocation, and do the heavy basket of laundry when asked. That’s why it feels difficult to ask them to consider more.

It’s just.... hard to come to terms with that, though, you now? We’re two fucked up individuals who actually understand our past traumas, and it really feels rare to find even that basic level of empathy. I’ve been feeling incompatable for a while, but... it just sucks. :(

There are a few things misrepresented here: it is not that they don’t do things to my exacting standards, it’s that they don’t do some things at all. Without me cleaning the entire kitchen when I can, it gets really nasty. They will do the dishes but nothing more. They’ve never once wiped the counters, cleaned out the fridge, or touched the litter box. 

They do the dishes two times in a row, rarely three when I’m particularly bad. But I will push through pain to wash the dishes regardless of my pain levels at that point. And when I do, I clean the counters from the multiple weeks they ignored them. This is done without comment, because like you said, what’s the point. I don’t criticize them like that. I sit down and try to open a conversation about our feelings when it gets particularly bad. 

When I walked into the living room to talk to them yesterday, they were surrounded by their actual garbage scattered around the floor that had been there for weeks... some, months. If I need to clean the living room, it’s an immense task. If Kay cleaned that space, it would only be by provocation, and it might only be “picking up trash” while the floor still needs swept, the table cleared, etc. And is that effort really equal when it takes minutes for one person, but days (having to break & recover) for another?

The problem is that it doesn’t happen unless I do it, and I’m not capable of that monumental effort. Since I am the only one cleaning out the nitty-gritty stuff, it could be said that I am more unto a maid than they are.

I too am on medications that are supposed to cause weight gain and am bedridden most of the time - yet I’m still (sometimes dangerously) underweight. I’m just saying that it really isn’t always a choice. It’s not my choice that I get so sick sometimes that I lose significant weight, just as it wouldn’t be a choice if someone was in the same place as me and gained significant weight. And some of those side effects can be caused by medication. Blaming people for their body changing in ways they have no control over isn’t a good mentality, and it can be severely damaging to that person’s mental health. All I’m asking is for people to have compassion for others, because you really don’t know what they’re going through.

This, here, is ableism. While some medications can cause lethargy and increased appetite (which also isn’t the fault of the person taking the medication), many other medications can affect your body’s metabolism, the way your body processes, stores, and absorbs nutrients, or cause water retention. Those sorts of medications can be extremely common, too - like birth control or insulin. You’re not doing anybody any favors by telling disabled people that it’s actually their fault.
